reader.notes: Every carrier of these functions now selects through the one kernel CobolIntrinsics.Selection.cs#ExtremeIndex (start at index 0, replace only on a strictly greater or strictly smaller comparison, so the leftmost of equal values is kept; ORD-* add 1): the exact-value lane through ExactOrder (CobolExact.Compare, algebraic value) since kb/Work PB6055 deleted SelectExact, and the aligned 256-bit lane through WideOrder since the same branch deleted SelectWide. Probes x1, x2 and x3 at --std 85 on the branch build print the same output at --std 2023; the generated C# shows OrdMaxExact, OrdMinExact, MaxExact and MinExact (NUMVAL, SQRT, power and mixed-scale arguments) and OrdMaxWide and OrdMinWide (power arguments) reached. A re-read of the kb/Work PB6053 record after PB6055 moved the code.

refuter.evidence: Code read independently at the pin: ExtremeIndex (Selection.cs) is the only selection loop left in Runtime/Intrinsics (a grep for a second leftmost-strict loop finds none once SelectExact and SelectWide are deleted); ExactOrder.Compare is CobolExact.Compare (big, SDIDI and wide forms compared by value, a mixed pair widened, never ordered by sign), WideOrder.Compare is CompareAligned (one scale: the emitter aligned the list). Edition: no Edition, DialectLevel or CobolVersion read on the selection path (the renderer's sites are the domain rule's citation and the standard-intermediate rounding, neither reachable for these functions at 85). Attacks past the reader's probes: x3.cob at --std 85 (exact lane with NUMVAL, SQRT, 18-digit and power arguments) printed Z1 01, Z2 01, Z3 03, Z4 01 (-0 vs -0.0 vs 0), Z5 01, Z6 .2500, Z7 01, Z8 03, Z9 2.9990, as RV1 to RV3 and the simple-condition rules require; x4.cob --compile-only refused mixed numeric and alphanumeric (COBOL1627 citing §1989:A.2.33.3 and §1989:A.2.32.3) and the 2002 empty list (COBOL0900; class c, a later edition's form refused at 85); x1, x2 and x3 identical at --std 2023.
